segments.text: Naṣb. When does a word end in fatha?
Some words in a verb sentence answer a question about the action.
What? Why? When? Where? How?
Those words take naṣb.
Chapter one. Where we are.
There are four cases. We know two. Today we add the third.
Case A is rafʿ, with damma. We have learned it.
Case B is naṣb, with fatha. This is the new one we add today.
Case C is jarr, with kasra. We have learned this one too.
Case D is called
جَزْم
Its sign is sukūn. It is for verbs. It comes later.
Only past verbs. For example, he wrote.
كَتَبَ
And order verbs. For example, write!
اُكْتُبْ
Present verbs come later.
And only one sign of naṣb: the fatha, alone or with tanween.
The other signs, for the dual and some plurals, come later in the course. Each group gets its own lesson.
Chapter two. A new sentence: the verb sentence.
Last lesson, the sentence started with a noun. Topic, then information.
Now it starts with a verb. Verb, then doer.
First, the verb. A past verb and an order verb are fixed.
مَبْنِيّ
Their ending never changes. A past verb ends in fatha.
كَتَبَ
An order verb ends in sukūn.
اُكْتُبْ
Then the doer. The doer is the one who did the action.
It takes rafʿ, with damma, like the topic.
With an order verb, the doer is you. It is hidden inside the verb.
Example A. Zayd wrote.
كَتَبَ زَيْدٌ
First, the verb. Wrote. It is a past verb, so it is fixed.
Its fatha never changes.
Who wrote?
زَيْدٌ
Zayd. That is the doer, so it takes rafʿ, with damma.
Listen to the ending once more.
كَتَبَ زَيْدٌ
Example B. Write!
اُكْتُبْ
This is an order verb. It is fixed on sukūn.
Who should write?
You. The doer is hidden inside the verb.
Careful. Look at the fatha on this verb.
كَتَبَ
That fatha is not naṣb.
A past verb ends in fatha in every sentence.
It is fixed.
Naṣb is for nouns.
Chapter three. The sign of naṣb: fatha.
It works just like damma and kasra. With al, or when owned, it takes one vowel. Otherwise, it takes tanween.
First card. With al, or when the word is owned, it takes one fatha only. No tanween.
With al, like the lesson.
الدَّرْسَ
Or owned, like the teacher's book.
كِتَابَ المُدَرِّسِ
Book is owned, so it takes one fatha.
Second card. No al. Fatha with tanween, written with an extra alif.
كِتَابًا
صَبَاحًا
Third card. The exception.
Some words end in a round ta, or in alif and hamza. They still take fatha with tanween. But there is no extra alif.
رَغْبَةً
مَسَاءً
Chapter four. Colour key: the new jobs.
A big box is the word's job in the sentence. A small box is a word with its own rule.
Navy is the verb. The action. Past and order verbs are fixed.
Orange is the doer. Who did the action? It takes rafʿ, with damma.
The four new jobs all take naṣb.
Pink is the object. What? Whom? The thing the action falls on.
Teal is the purpose. Why? The reason for the action.
Brown is time or place. When? Where? With no preposition.
Olive is the state. How? The state of the doer or object.
The small boxes from last lesson still work. After a preposition. Ownership. Adjective. And after wa.
Chapter five. The four naṣb jobs at a glance.
Find the verb and the doer. For every other noun, ask the question. The one it answers is its job.
Object. What? Whom? The thing the action falls on. The student wrote the lesson.
كَتَبَ الطَّالِبُ الدَّرْسَ
Purpose. Why? The reason. Usually an action noun with tanween. The student stood up out of respect.
وَقَفَ الطَّالِبُ احْتِرَامًا
Time or place. When? Where? No preposition. Zayd travelled in the morning.
سَافَرَ زَيْدٌ صَبَاحًا
State. How? The state of the doer or object, with no al. Zayd came hurrying.
جَاءَ زَيْدٌ مُسْرِعًا
Chapter six. The object.
مَفْعُولٌ بِهِ
Here is the rule. The object is the thing the action falls on.
cues: hl:the thing the action falls on

segments.text: To find it, ask what, or whom, after the verb.
The object takes naṣb. Its sign is fatha.
Example one. The student wrote the lesson.
كَتَبَ الطَّالِبُ الدَّرْسَ
First, the verb. Wrote. It is a past verb, so it is fixed.
Who wrote?
الطَّالِبُ
The student. That is the doer, so it takes damma.
What did he write?
الدَّرْسَ
The lesson. That is the object, so it ends in fatha.
Listen to the ending once more.
كَتَبَ الطَّالِبُ الدَّرْسَ
Example two. Zayd read a book.
قَرَأَ زَيْدٌ كِتَابًا
The verb is fixed, and Zayd is the doer, with damma and tanween.
What did he read?
كِتَابًا
A book. It is the object.
It has no al. So it takes fatha with tanween, and an extra alif.
Example three. Open the door!
اِفْتَحِ البَابَ
This is an order verb. It is fixed.
اِفْتَحِ
Hear the kasra on its end. It is only a bridge to al. It is not a case ending.
The doer is hidden. It is you.
Open what?
البَابَ
The door. That is the object, so it ends in fatha.
Example four. The student read the teacher's book.
قَرَأَ الطَّالِبُ كِتَابَ المُدَرِّسِ
The verb is fixed, and the doer takes damma.
What did he read?
كِتَابَ
It is the object, so it ends in fatha.
But it is owned. So it has no tanween.
المُدَرِّسِ
Book of the teacher. The teacher is the owner. The owner takes kasra.
A tip. An order verb that ends in sukūn takes a small kasra before al.
اِفْتَحِ البَابَ
اِشْرَبِ المَاءَ
The verb is still fixed.
Chapter seven. Purpose.
مَفْعُولٌ لِأَجْلِهِ
The purpose gives the reason for the action.
cues: hl:gives the reason for the action

segments.text: To find it, ask why.
It is usually an action noun with tanween, like respect, desire, or seeking.
Purpose takes naṣb, so it ends in fatha.
Example five. The student stood up out of respect.
وَقَفَ الطَّالِبُ احْتِرَامًا
First, the verb. Stood up. It is a past verb, so it is fixed.
Who stood up?
الطَّالِبُ
The student. That is the doer, so it takes damma.
Why did he stand?
احْتِرَامًا
Out of respect. That is the purpose, so it takes fatha with tanween.
Listen to the ending once more.
وَقَفَ الطَّالِبُ احْتِرَامًا
Example six. Zayd studied out of desire for success.
دَرَسَ زَيْدٌ رَغْبَةً فِي النَّجَاحِ
The verb is fixed, and the doer takes damma.
Why did he study?
رَغْبَةً
Out of desire. The purpose, so fatha with tanween.
It ends in a round ta, so there is no extra alif.
النَّجَاحِ
Success. The small word before it means in. So success comes after a preposition, and it takes kasra.
Example seven. Ali travelled seeking knowledge.
سَافَرَ عَلِيٌّ طَلَبًا لِلْعِلْمِ
The verb is fixed. Ali is the doer, with damma.
Why did he travel?
طَلَبًا
Seeking. The purpose, so fatha with tanween.
لِلْعِلْمِ
This word has two parts. The first part means for. It is a small preposition.
العِلْمِ
Knowledge. It comes after a preposition, so it takes kasra.
A tip. Object or purpose? Ask the question.
قَرَأَ زَيْدٌ كِتَابًا
What did he read?
A book. That is the object.
وَقَفَ زَيْدٌ احْتِرَامًا
Why did he stand?
Out of respect. That is the purpose.
Chapter eight. Time or place.
مَفْعُولٌ فِيهِ
A time or place word tells us when or where the action happened.
cues: hl:when or where the action happened

segments.text: It has no preposition.
Ask when, or where.
Time or place takes naṣb, so it ends in fatha.
Example eight. Zayd travelled in the morning.
سَافَرَ زَيْدٌ صَبَاحًا
First, the verb. Travelled. It is a past verb, so it is fixed.
Who travelled?
زَيْدٌ
Zayd. That is the doer, so it takes damma.
When did he travel?
صَبَاحًا
In the morning. That is time, so it takes fatha with tanween.
Listen to the ending once more.
سَافَرَ زَيْدٌ صَبَاحًا
Example nine. The boy came back in the evening.
رَجَعَ الوَلَدُ مَسَاءً
The verb is fixed, and the doer takes damma.
When did he come back?
مَسَاءً
In the evening. Time, so fatha with tanween.
It ends in alif and hamza, so no extra alif.
Example ten. The student sat in front of the teacher.
جَلَسَ الطَّالِبُ أَمَامَ المُدَرِّسِ
The verb is fixed, and the doer takes damma.
Where did he sit?
أَمَامَ
In front of. Place, so fatha. It is owned, so no tanween.
المُدَرِّسِ
In front of the teacher. The teacher is the owner, so kasra.
Example eleven. Sit under the tree!
اِجْلِسْ تَحْتَ الشَّجَرَةِ
An order verb, so it is fixed. The doer is hidden. It is you.
Sit where?
تَحْتَ
Under. Place, so fatha, and it is owned.
الشَّجَرَةِ
The owner takes kasra.
Example twelve. Ali went out on Friday.
خَرَجَ عَلِيٌّ يَوْمَ الجُمُعَةِ
The verb is fixed, and the doer takes damma.
When did he go out?
يَوْمَ
On the day of Friday. Time, so fatha, and it is owned.
الجُمُعَةِ
The owner takes kasra.
A tip. No preposition means naṣb.
جَلَسَ زَيْدٌ أَمَامَ البَيْتِ
No preposition here.
أَمَامَ
So it takes fatha.
جَلَسَ زَيْدٌ فِي البَيْتِ
Now the house comes after a preposition, so it takes kasra.
Chapter nine. The state.
حَال
The state tells us how the doer, or the object, was during the action.
cues: hl:tells us how the doer (or the object) was during the action

segments.text: To find it, ask how.
It has no al, so it almost always takes tanween.
The state takes naṣb, so it ends in fatha.
Example thirteen. Zayd came hurrying.
جَاءَ زَيْدٌ مُسْرِعًا
First, the verb. Came. It is a past verb, so it is fixed.
Who came?
زَيْدٌ
Zayd. The doer, so damma with tanween.
How did he come?
مُسْرِعًا
Hurrying. That is the state, so fatha with tanween.
Listen to the ending once more.
جَاءَ زَيْدٌ مُسْرِعًا
Example fourteen. The boy came back happy.
رَجَعَ الوَلَدُ فَرِحًا
The verb is fixed, and the doer takes damma.
How did he come back?
فَرِحًا
Happy. A state, so fatha with tanween.
Example fifteen. The student entered the class smiling.
دَخَلَ الطَّالِبُ الصَّفَّ مُبْتَسِمًا
The verb is fixed, and the doer takes damma.
Entered what?
الصَّفَّ
The class. The object, so fatha.
How did he enter?
مُبْتَسِمًا
Smiling. The state, so fatha with tanween.
Example sixteen. Drink the water cold!
اِشْرَبِ المَاءَ بَارِدًا
An order verb, so it is fixed. The doer is hidden. It is you.
Drink what?
المَاءَ
The water. The object, so fatha.
How should the water be?
بَارِدًا
Cold. Here the state describes the object, the water. So it takes fatha with tanween.
A tip. State or adjective?
جَاءَ الطَّالِبُ المُسْرِعُ
The hurrying student came. The last word has al, so it is an adjective. It copies the damma of the student.
جَاءَ الطَّالِبُ مُسْرِعًا
The student came hurrying. Now the last word has no al, so it is a state. It takes naṣb.
Chapter ten. Old rules, new ending.
An adjective and a word after wa still copy. Now they can copy a fatha.
Example seventeen. Zayd read a new book.
قَرَأَ زَيْدٌ كِتَابًا جَدِيدًا
The verb is fixed. Zayd is the doer, with damma and tanween.
What did he read?
كِتَابًا
A book. The object, so fatha with tanween.
جَدِيدًا
New. It describes the book, so it copies. Fatha with tanween.
Listen to both endings once more.
قَرَأَ زَيْدٌ كِتَابًا جَدِيدًا
Example eighteen. The student wrote the lesson and the homework.
كَتَبَ الطَّالِبُ الدَّرْسَ وَالوَاجِبَ
The verb is fixed. The doer takes damma.
What did he write?
الدَّرْسَ
The lesson. The object, so fatha.
وَالوَاجِبَ
And the homework. It comes after wa, so it copies the lesson. Fatha.
Chapter eleven. All together.
Example nineteen. The teacher opened the door in the morning.
فَتَحَ المُدَرِّسُ البَابَ صَبَاحًا
The verb is fixed.
Who opened?
المُدَرِّسُ
The teacher. The doer, so damma.
Opened what?
البَابَ
The door. The object, so fatha.
When did he open it?
صَبَاحًا
In the morning. Time, so fatha with tanween.
Listen to the endings once more.
فَتَحَ المُدَرِّسُ البَابَ صَبَاحًا
Example twenty. Ali travelled at night seeking knowledge.
سَافَرَ عَلِيٌّ لَيْلًا طَلَبًا لِلْعِلْمِ
The verb is fixed. Ali is the doer, with damma and tanween.
When did he travel?
لَيْلًا
At night. Time, so fatha with tanween.
Why did he travel?
طَلَبًا
Seeking. Purpose, so fatha with tanween.
لِلْعِلْمِ
For knowledge. The small part at the front means for. It is a preposition, so knowledge takes kasra.
Example twenty-one. The hardworking student sat in front of the teacher, smiling.
جَلَسَ الطَّالِبُ المُجْتَهِدُ أَمَامَ المُدَرِّسِ مُبْتَسِمًا
The verb is fixed.
الطَّالِبُ
The student. The doer, so damma.
المُجْتَهِدُ
Hardworking. It describes the doer, so it copies damma.
Where did he sit?
أَمَامَ
In front of. Place, so fatha. It is owned, so no tanween.
المُدَرِّسِ
The teacher. It is the owner, so it takes kasra.
How did he sit?
مُبْتَسِمًا
Smiling. State, so fatha with tanween.
This one uses almost every colour.
Verb and doer first. Then ask what, why, when, where, or how for the rest.
Five questions find every ending.
One. Is it a verb or a particle? Then it is fixed. It never changes.
Two. Is it a topic, information, or a doer? Then damma.
Three. Does it answer what, why, when, where, or how? Then fatha.
Four. Does it come after a preposition, or is it the owner? Then kasra.
Five. Is it an adjective, or after wa? Then copy the word it follows.

Eight sentences. Every ending is missing.
Find the verb and the doer first. Then box every other job. For an order, write its hidden doer.
For every word, circle its ending and its job. Write the reason in your notebook.
Work alone, then check with a partner and the answer key.
